Aisha: quick sync — saw tenant `acme-inc` route to a cost-unsafe model variant during yesterday's EU->US failover. looks like policy deltas applied in different orders across regions and produced non-deterministic penalties. anyone else seen this?

Ben: yep, reproduced locally. when two policy writes land concurrently we end up with non-commutative penalty updates (A then B != B then A). runtimes make short-lived decisions and the mismatch shows up as extra hedges. :facepalm:

Carlos: one obvious approach is to attach a monotonic `policy_epoch` to the compiled policy bundle. runtime prefers decisions from the highest epoch; when epoch increments we atomically swap the bundle. keeps decision logic simple at runtime.

Danielle: epoch is neat but doesn't solve concurrent bumps from independent controllers. we could use a vector-clock per-namespace: each controller increments its axis, publish vector, and runtime resolves with a merge rule (e.g., prefer highest sum or lexicographic). more resilient to partitions but adds runtime compare complexity.

Ben: vector clocks add a lot of cognitive load and storage. simpler alternative: a sequencer service that assigns a strictly increasing apply-ts to deltas (global order). sequencer gives total order guarantees which makes merges deterministic. downside: single-point-of-availability unless we shard/replicate and accept tail latency.

Aisha: tradeoffs summary — sequencer = deterministic & easy to reason about, availability risk; epoch/vector = more distributed but complex merge semantics. could we do a hybrid: local epoch per-region for availability + a cross-region reconciliation pass that reorders deltas into a canonical sequence and marks 'compatibility window' for in-flight requests? while reconcile is running, runtimes set `compat_mode: gradual` so old decisions keep a fallback.

Carlos: sketch of the hybrid config (POC):
```json
{
  "policy_bundle": "pricing-2026-11",
  "policy_epoch": 42,
  "compat_mode": "gradual",
  "compat_window_secs": 60
}
```
runtime: attach header `x-policy-epoch: 42` to decision telemetry. when header mismatches with reconciled canonical epoch, runtime yields to `compat_fallback` for existing sessions.

Danielle: ops needs observability before we try this in prod: add trace tag `policy_digest` to every decision, metric `policy_mismatch_rate`, and alert if mismatch > 0.5% for 10m. also a rollback playbook: how to force all regions to the last-good epoch.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout: policy-svc v1.4.1 -> eu1 (canary 5%), us-west (canary 5%). monitor `policy_mismatch_rate`.

Aisha: action items — (1) POC hybrid: local epoch + reconciliation job (Carlos + Ben) (2) add `policy_digest` traces & `policy_mismatch_rate` metric (Danielle) (3) draft runbook + RFC for rollout/rollback behavior (Aisha). I'll capture RFC notes and spin up a doc. :thumbsup: 

Ben: I'll bench a lightweight sequencer implementation so we can compare latency/availability at 95/99p. gist with microbench coming in thread. :eyes:

Carlos: I'll start the reconcile-job sketch and a tiny runtime opt-in flag `compat_mode=gradual` so we can test in canary.

Danielle: will add alerts and dashboard tiles to the console once the trace keys are wired.

Aisha: great. keeping this tight — short RFC by EOD tomorrow and small canary next week. thanks everyone. :rocket:
